title: Record of the Return
summary: Three weeks of keeping Jing. Gotō brings Jing to a southern city, from job-hunting and the docks to the break.

frames.label: About this record
frames.text: Extra: three weeks of keeping Jing. 2025.08.28~09.21, a southern city. Gotō takes Jing in -> denial -> the docks -> rupture. Gender issues are only sketched; Gotō's denials and self-account are his perspective, not the truth; place names are generalized; no interpretation is added.
August 28, night

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Jing's mother called out of nowhere, worried about where Jing had gone, suspecting she'd o'd or drunk and gone out.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I called her on voice, and the moment I heard that mouth like mashed radish, I knew she'd o'd or been drinking again.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Jing turned on video and showed she was sitting in the open ground floor of her building. I told her to go home, but her ears might as well have been stuffed with wool.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I had to contact her mother. Round and round, and finally her mother found her; only then did I breathe out.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Jing's mother complained that Jing locks her door all day and won't come out, won't come when called, won't eat.
Jing's mother and Gotō agreed: Jing had to be pulled to the southern city, find a job, be changed.
Her mother has her own work and can't look after a twenty-one-year-old with no job all day. Jing had to change her environment, get off the drugs, and find work too. Vocational school education, an adult for three years already.
September 4, noon

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Jing arrived.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: Do I look weird like this?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I think you just overthink things. Stop chewing on this all day.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Gotō first took her for a bowl of rice noodles, then dropped the luggage and settled in.
By evening Jing went out for air and didn't come back for two hours.
Gotō went downstairs and ran a kilometre there and back looking for her, and finally found her at the bus stop.
Jing was crying nonstop, chattering away, head in her hands going uh-ah-ah-ah.
Two patrol officers got out and asked her: been drinking?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: She just came out for some air.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
So it was Gotō's opening 'you overthink' that set her off.
Gotō and Jing talked back and forth for five hours, from those anxieties to childhood memories, and at least got her talked back to sleep.
Next Jing looked for a rental; eight days passed, until September 12, before she found one.
In between Jing cut her hair and got her nails done.
Gotō phoned the grandmother and mother up north for supplies, and found that mother assumed father would send, and father assumed mother would.
September 12, night

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Jing o'd pregabalin again.
Gotō grabbed a long stick and hurried over, only to find Jing already acting out, barely able to walk.
He bought tea and fed it to her, trying to make her throw it up, but she only brought up a little, because it had been digesting for an hour.
He called a car to take her to the riverside docks; on the lawn he showed her the stars, the bridge and the cranes, talked at random to comfort her, and reasoned with her anxiety.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: After od I get persecutory delusions. I think Gotō wants to hurt me.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
On the lawn Jing cursed her mother for making her like this.
Gotō didn't understand those ideas of hers, and couldn't support her thinking all day long without a proper job.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: My obsessive thinking is severe. I need pregabalin for it.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Gotō remembered his own teens: food cut off, power cut off, temperature control cut off; winter 2019 with no quilt and no heating, sleeping on a board bed with a bamboo mat, and by the spirit of struggle he hasn't o'd since.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I can't do that. I still have to look after this one... fuck, I really raised a living ancestor.
September 15

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Jing got her ears pierced, and bought little trinkets.
Gotō invited her out for Tastien, to see the night market.
Watching Jing lean in close to those little earrings, something uncomfortable rose in him: pity for the iron that won't become steel, eleven days and not a single job hunted.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: The base determines the superstructure. Find a job first, then talk about the rest.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Jing broke down.
September 16, 6:47 a.m.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: Goodbye, teacher.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: At 7:19 Gotō opened his phone and saw this line.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: He called voice immediately. She picked up, and he only heard Jing moaning; three seconds later three men's voices mixed in.

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: Hello, are you her friend?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Yes. What's going on with her now?

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: Your friend seems drunk. She's collapsed at the docks.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Huh? Where?

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: The docks. Can you come now?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Fuck fuck fuck I'm on my way!

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Gotō burst out the door, grabbed a shared bike, ran several red lights, and raced eight kilometres in half an hour to the docks.
Past the cover of the trees, he saw something in the shade from a distance. It was Jing, collapsed here.

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: You're her friend, right? God, we're exhausted. She passed out and won't wake at all.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Fuck, what do we do?

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: We just called the station. The officer didn't even want to come. Does she have other family?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: No. She's from out of town. Here I'm the only person she knows.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Gotō tried calling Jing; she didn't react at all. He pulled at her, and her whole body was like a sack packed with potatoes and water, slamming straight onto the ground.

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: You'd better not try pulling her. Someone this completely drunk is like a dead pig, very hard to move. It took all three of us to move her.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: A young dock worker handed over a cup of water and tried to give it to her.

frames.name: Dock Worker
frames.text: Did she take something? Why is there a pile of pills in her bag?

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Gotō opened her bag: blister packs shoved in every which way, pregabalin, dextromethorphan, and also clonazepam and sodium valproate.
He opened her phone: Jing had joined a suicide group for some reason, and Gotō had known nothing about it.
The chat logs showed Jing had been sitting at the dock edge for those two hours, planning to fall into the river once the drugs came on. But she couldn't fall; the dock workers found her and held her back.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I'll call a taxi to take her home.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
The taxi arrived, and Gotō, the dock workers and the driver together hauled Jing's utterly irresponsible, scattered body into the car.
On the way Gotō couldn't think anymore. He'd slept three hours and been woken twice, hadn't eaten the night before, the only thing he'd eaten was a compressed biscuit before he opened his phone, hadn't drunk water either, and his whole body was soaked in sweat.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I still have to be responsible. I still have to lead her. I can't fall.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: When I fall, will anyone handle the aftermath for me? Why is it always me handling the aftermath for other people?

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
At the apartment building, that corridor was a full fifty metres. Dragging her along the floor risked the friction hurting her skin, pulling her by the hands couldn't lift her, carrying her on his back wouldn't fit her shoulders, and holding her was out of the question.
Gotō hoisted Jing's upper body and dragged her into the lift. Door open, dragged her out the same way.
He worked out an angle and put Jing's arm over his shoulder. Up — no, that angle won't do; another one — ah, good, I'm standing.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: You only hate how little strength you have when you need it.

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
He ran with all his might, like running through deep-water cement, and finally arrived.
With the last of his strength he rolled Jing onto the bed like a steamed fish and put her in the recovery position.
When it was done he was drenched, shaking all over, his legs weak, staring blankly at the ceiling, and collapsed into sleep.
September 16, evening

frames.label: Record
frames.text:
Jing woke a little.
Jing resented that the dock workers shouldn't have helped her.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: So the ones who helped you are wrong, and the ones who indulged you are right?

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Gotō talked some ideology with her. She didn't accept it.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: She genuinely does no labour, and is full of idealism.
September 17, night

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: Teacher says buying things I like, wearing things I like, looking the way I like, is wrong.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: It's teacher opposing me that gave me such a shock and made me break down.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: I don't want to argue with teacher. I just want teacher to know what I'm thinking. I'm going to sleep.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Think about it after you've worked for a while.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: The you I imagined has shattered. Goodbye, teacher.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: I can't take any more shocks.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: ??? I won't cover for everything you do.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I'm not your lover or your partner. In the end I'm just here to lead you off od and get you a job.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: Gotō found a delivery job that looked decent and sent it to her, then went off to play Delta Force and stopped bothering with her.
September 19

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: Let's each be well. We have no relationship anymore — not teacher and student, not friends. That's it.

frames.name: Jing
frames.text: I hope you can become independent soon too.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Test.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Does that mean I can finally get rid of this fucking nuisance?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: And what's this 'become independent soon'? She's still living off her mother's money, not working, not treating her illness.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Forget it, why should I bother with her? Anyway I've finally seen off this number-one plague.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I finally have my own time to catch up on study, play games, look at cats. Great. Hurry up and get lost, I'm going to the park.

frames.label: Record
frames.text: For three days Gotō couldn't have been happier. Nothing to look after, only himself.

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: I could clearly just throw all this off. What do the circle's business and I have to do with each other? Isn't gaming nicer?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: My friends are cleaner too, every one of them normal. I'm very happy.
September 21, afternoon

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: Huh? She's thrown in with the enemy?

frames.name: Gotō
frames.text: What do you mean I'm hurting her? What do you mean I pua'd her?
